story: Kenya's elections have been decided by ethnic coalitions since multiparty politics returned in 1992, and the most important bloc is Mount Kenya, home to the Kikuyu, the largest community. William Ruto won in 2022 by bringing Mount Kenya with him through his running mate, Rigathi Gachagua. Then in 2024, Gen Z protesters stormed parliament over tax rises, dozens were killed, and Ruto's allies impeached Gachagua. The result in 2026: the man who delivered Ruto his key votes is now organising to take them away.

Gachagua has joined Kalonzo Musyoka, Martha Karua, former interior minister Fred Matiang'i and others in a United Opposition pledged to field one candidate against Ruto in August 2027 and hold him to a single term (Capital FM via AllAfrica). "If the mountain votes as a bloc, he stands no chance," Gachagua said in February (The Star). The death of Raila Odinga, the veteran opposition leader, in October 2025 left his western base up for grabs, and Matiang'i is courting it. But unity is fragile: Musyoka wanted the candidate named by March, Gachagua wants to wait until December 2026, and Karua has objected to Gachagua being treated as the coalition's leader (Nation). Ruto's party won all three Mount Kenya by-elections this year, which the opposition called rigged. The opposition also attacked the government for letting young Kenyans be recruited to fight for Russia.
briefing.power: A presidential republic under the 2010 constitution. The president is directly elected for five years with a two-term limit and must win half the vote plus a quarter in at least 24 of 47 counties; parliament has a National Assembly and Senate, and counties have elected governors.
